RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone is almost no evidence. In economics, all-women panels are uncommon, but women are overrepresented in service and committee work, so this happens often without bias. Raising it would frame you as someone who suspects women of favouring women — which damages your credibility and distracts from your actual, stronger point.

That point is the credential gap: completed PhD versus unfinished, six papers versus two. That's a legitimate question about how criteria were weighted — though "industry experience" and teaching demos are genuinely valued, and the announcement won't reflect the full file.

Pursue the written explanation instead. Two weeks' silence is the concrete problem. Resend in writing, cite any policy or statutory right to reasons, copy HR.
